analysis.title: GS Ellinikaki - 10 for the weekend (23 Oct 2026)
key_insights: Second week of AI/momentum derisking, with the rotation likely to have further to run. The high-velocity selling may be behind us, but midterms, DC build out and issuance should keep the backdrop choppy. Relief on energy (and hence rates) could open a meaningful right tail.

META, SPCX and LRCX delivered strong numbers, token consumption is accelerating, B200 pricing is breaking out, and SpaceX cited sub-1 year paybacks on new compute. Investors are focused on whether the industry can deliver the forecast capacity build out, whether returns justify the capex, and how much compute is needed as inference efficiency improves.
Feedback this week was that, absent relief on energy, rates or geopolitics, it is hard to see a catalyst for broader re-risking ahead of the midterms.
The SOX underperformed the S&P 500 by 13% over nine sessions, its worst relative stretch in 20+ years, and is testing its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2025.

On Thursday all three major equity HF strategies fell more than 1% on the same day for the first time since COVID: Fundamentals -1.1%, Systematic -1.2%, Multi-Strats -1.4%. The Systematic and Multi-Strats moves were -3.2 SD and -2.5 SD respectively.

Rotation continued, with US Staples outperforming the Nasdaq YTD. GS baskets team: High Beta Momentum is down 43% from its June peak, erasing all YTD gains, and is in its worst drawdown since the GFC outside COVID.
The broadening trade is working: S&P 500 ex-AI outperformed the S&P by 6pp in October, with rotation toward quality in 2H.

GIR work on slowing growth: after months of pressure from higher rates, rising costs of capital are feeding into lower equity growth expectations. Cyclicals vs Defensives fell 6% since the start of the month, amplified by reduced positioning, with similar growth concerns in rates and credit.
META showed strong fundamentals alone are not enough. The debate is now AI spend, monetisation and the path to peak capex/FCF pressure (Eric Sheridan).
Next week's hyperscaler prints are flagged as critical: focus on backlog conversion, deployment and funding, and whether AI investment delivers attractive returns.

GS Credit Research: recent spread widening is concentrated in neoclouds and companies with frontier lab/project finance exposure. Three key risks to underwrite are construction, coverage/refinancing and the strength of the underlying hyperscaler lease.
European capital goods results were strong (ABB +40% organic orders YoY, Atlas Copco +25%, Metso +24%, Sandvik +17%), but none closed higher on the print in a risk-off tape.

In civil aerospace the bear case broadened beyond risk-off. Safran crystallised idiosyncratic concerns on capex, growth and cash flow, leaving crowded civil aero/aftermarket names like Rolls Royce vulnerable to further rotation out of the sector.

Long idea into next week: ABI ahead of results, with beat potential (+4.5% organic EBITDA vs +3.9% consensus), the transactional headwind turning into a Q4 tailwind, and scope for a 100% increase in the interim dividend.
Metals & Mining conference feedback: LME week saw an 'astonishingly bearish position observed by all'. The last big commodity cycle was demand driven, this cycle is supply driven (James McGeouch).
